title: Choose a retrieval approach
summary: Start from existing interfaces and the data model before comparing products.

sections.label: Use what is already available
sections.text: If an approved API returns the required information, record its contract and validation needs first. A database replacement is a separate architecture decision.

sections.label: Different families
sections.text: These entries illustrate different models and interfaces. They do not establish drop-in compatibility, pricing, performance or availability in your environment.

sections.label: Your existing tool
sections.text: In Factory, record your component technology and its version. A custom technology is allowed when it is absent from the list. Generic guidance remains available without a specialist compatibility claim.

sections.label: Gap review: workflow use and checks
items: Recommended workflow use: Architecture and impact, Compare feasible approaches, Plan the evidence. Use when an information need requires an interface or data-model decision, comparing feasible alternatives and planning a bounded comparison. This is an Atlas recommendation reviewed on 2026-10-15, not a mandatory process or an observed execution result.
Check output to obtain: Record the existing approved interface, required result and missing capability before considering a replacement.
Check output to obtain: For each relevant alternative, document its actual data model, query contract and project constraints without claiming drop-in compatibility.
Check output to obtain: Define representative queries, expected results and cost or maintenance measurements before collecting observations.

confidence: Documented facts have scoped sources. Suitability for a particular project remains unverified.

catalog.applicability: Use when choosing between an existing approved API and a relational, RDF or property graph store for a retrieval need. Record the interface contract and validation needs first, a database replacement is a separate architecture decision.
catalog.limits: This is design guidance. It does not connect to a service or prove that a result is correct.

claims.text: The named examples document SQL, SPARQL or Cypher in the respective data models.
